haiku-low.q1: They still reach the same linked account, matched by Google sub. Google never changes the stored email, which stays untouched.
haiku-low.q2: The user must enter that account's password at /auth/google/confirm. A correct password links the Google account, then start_session creates the session.
haiku-low.q3: Each wrong password increments failed_logins. At 5, the account locks for 15 minutes and the pending link is deleted, so the user must restart from /login.
haiku-low.q4: Unmatched verified email: a new user is created with NULL password and a google_identities row, then a session starts. Unverified email: refused, sent to email and password login, nothing created.
haiku-low.q5: NOT STATED for a duplicate callback beyond: state is consumed on first read. After 12 minutes the Redis key has expired. Both give a generic error page linking to /login, with nothing changed.
haiku-low.q6: start_session: deletes any old sid row, inserts a new sessions row, and sets a new sid cookie. The old sid row is removed and replaced.
haiku-low.q7: No password or email match is required, but the signed-in user must equal the stored user_id. If that Google account is linked to someone else, the link is refused.
haiku-low.q8: In Redis key oidc:state:<state>, set with 600s TTL. The oidc_bind cookie holds the state. Removed by GETDEL on first callback, or expires at 600s; cookie cleared on callback.
haiku-low.q9: Held in Redis oidc:pending:<id> with sub, user_id and next. The browser refers to it by the random g_pending cookie id. Deleted on link success, lock, failed re-check, or 600s expiry.
haiku-low.q10: In PostgreSQL table google_identities. Primary key on sub limits a Google account to one user; UNIQUE user_id limits a user to one Google account.
haiku-low.q11: The user is returned to origin with Google sign-in failed, try again. The code is never retried; the state is consumed and the user starts a new attempt.
haiku-low.q12: The mode comes from the stored Redis state record, not the URL. Link mode requires the current sid user to equal the user_id stored at start.

sonnet.q1: They still reach the same account, because the link is by sub, not email. The sub is found in google_identities, so they sign in to the linked user and the stored email is untouched. Google never changes our stored email.
sonnet.q2: Callback finds the sub unlinked and the email verified, and it matches a user that has no Google link. The server creates a pending record in Redis (oidc:pending:ID, 600s) and sets the g_pending cookie. The user must then enter that account's password at /auth/google/confirm. If bcrypt matches (and the account isn't locked and the re-check passes), the identity is inserted, the pending record is deleted, and start_session runs.
sonnet.q3: Each wrong password adds 1 to failed_logins, and the form is shown again with the pending record and its TTL unchanged. At the fifth, locked_until = now + 15 min and failed_logins resets to 0. The pending record and g_pending cookie are then deleted, so the half-finished link is discarded. The user goes back to /login with 'Account temporarily locked' and must start over. If the account was already locked at confirm, the same drop happens.
sonnet.q4: Verified email with no matching user: one transaction creates a users row (password_hash NULL, email_verified_at = now) and a google_identities row, then start_session runs. Email not verified: refused and sent back to /login, telling them to use email and password. No user is created.
sonnet.q5: Both cases give the same outcome. After 12 minutes the state key has expired, and a second load finds the key already consumed by GETDEL. Either way it is a generic error page with a link to /login, and nothing changes.
sonnet.q6: The existing, normal session. start_session creates a sessions row and sets the sid cookie, with no new session type. It deletes any old sid row first, then redirects to next (if relative) or /home. In link mode there is no new session: the same session and sid stay, and the user returns to settings.
sonnet.q7: Neither. Link mode asks no password and the emails need not match. The signed-in user must equal the user_id stored at start. If that Google account (sub) is already linked to another user, it is refused with 'that Google account is linked to someone else'. A race is refused the same way, via the unique violation.
sonnet.q8: In the Redis record oidc:state:<state>, which holds code_verifier, nonce, mode, user_id (link mode only), origin and next. It is also tied to the oidc_bind cookie. The first callback read removes it through GETDEL (used at most once), or it expires after 600s. The oidc_bind cookie is cleared on every callback response, or expires with Max-Age 600.
sonnet.q9: It is held in the Redis record oidc:pending:<id>, which holds sub, user_id of the matched account, and next. The browser refers to it through the g_pending cookie, which holds the random 32-byte id. The record is deleted on successful link, on account lock, on a failed re-check, or at 600s. A wrong password does not extend the TTL. The cookie is cleared whenever the record is deleted.
sonnet.q10: In the PostgreSQL table google_identities (sub, user_id, linked_at). sub is the PRIMARY KEY, so one Google account links to at most one user. user_id is NOT NULL UNIQUE and references users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE, so one user has at most one Google account.
sonnet.q11: The user is returned to the origin with 'Google sign-in failed, try again'. Nothing is changed. The code exchange is not retried, because the state is consumed and a Google code is single-use, so the user must start a new attempt. A bad ID token is handled the same way.
sonnet.q12: The callback reads the mode from the stored Redis state record, never from the URL. For link mode, the record holds the user_id from the start. The callback checks that the current sid user equals that user_id. If not, it shows the generic error page and nothing changes.
